q: How does a paper mill count sludge and rejects in its footprint?
title: Paper mills: sludge and rejects
short: Burnt in your own boiler, they are Scope 1, with biogenic CO2 from fibre reported separately and CO2 from plastic rejects counted in full. Sent to a landfill or another company, they are Scope 3 category 5, waste generated in operations.
audience: Recycled and agro residue paper mills in India handling ETP sludge and pulper rejects

ul: Own boiler: fossil share of rejects, mainly plastics, in Scope 1; fibre share biogenic.
Landfill: Scope 3 category 5, using a factor for the waste type and disposal route.
Sold to a cement kiln or brick maker: category 5 only for any treatment you pay for.

p: Weighbridge slips for sludge and rejects leaving the site, and moisture content, because wet tonnes overstate the mass.
Plastic is fossil carbon. Burning it raises your Scope 1 even if the rest of the fuel is biomass.

senseible: Senseible reads the energy invoices behind the making stage into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, and keeps material invoices on the Scope 3 trail. Material factors come from your supplier or a named database and are labelled with their source, so the product figure can be traced line by line.
